description: MEASURED 2026-09-12. Edit repos/llm-resolver-vessel/src/index.ts. IMPLEMENTER NOTE, VERIFIED 2026-09-12: the existing llmModelPolicy_write shape accepts { arms?: PolicyArm[]; cost_weight?: number; merge?: boolean } and merges incoming arms by model name via Object.assign, bumping policy.rev and saving. It does NOT accept an outcome delta such as { model, reached }, so it cannot serve as the grading endpoint as-is. Two options, and the second is preferred. (a) Have the reach stage read the policy, adjust the selected arm's alpha or beta, and merge it back through llmModelPolicy_write - this works with zero new shapes but is READ-MODIFY-WRITE and therefore racy against concurrent graders, and it also lets any caller rewrite arbitrary arm fields. (b) Add a narrow shaped impulse whose payload is the execution id and the reached boolean, and have its handler call the already-written gradeArmByExecution, which performs the increment atomically against the pending ledger. Option (b) is a mint, but it is the justified kind: it is the missing reader for a write that already exists, and law 1 wants the grading verdict to arrive as a shape rather than as an out-of-band call. SECOND VERIFIED FACT THAT BOUNDS THE EXPECTED GAIN: fixing the grader is NECESSARY BUT NOT SUFFICIENT. llmQuotaState plus the resolver journal show that only chutes and openrouter authenticate; anthropic returns 401 authentication_error and is cooled down as a consequence, while groq, mistral and google have no key at all. So a correctly graded selector would still be choosing among the same five arms - gemini-2.5-flash, deepseek-chat-v3-0324, gpt-4o-mini, nemotron-3-nano-30b free and north-mini-code free. Grading fixes WHICH of those wins and stops the posterior from lying; it cannot introduce a stronger model that is not reachable. Note also that llmQuotaState's present flag means a key string is configured, not that it authenticates. DECISIVE EVIDENCE ADDED 2026-09-12, and it states the defect far more sharply than the summary above. The policy already implements PER-TASK-TYPE posteriors: each arm carries task_alpha and task_beta maps keyed by task type, and they are populated and working. Reading the live llmModelPolicy shape - 13 arms, rev 9 - the per-task posteriors exist for SEVEN task types: reach_verification on 8 arms, derivation_split_classification on 7, doctor_probe on 7, pointer_arg_extraction on 7, action_shape_selection on 7, terminal_content_process on 7, and goal_target_inference on 6. FOR THE TWO DRAFTING TASK TYPES THE COUNT IS ZERO: feature_compose 0 arms, patch_with_tools 0 arms. The mechanism works everywhere except the place that writes all the code. WHY, EXACTLY: the grading call site guards with 'if (!DRAFTING_TASK_TYPES.has(body.task_type ?? "") && !providerLevelFailure)', where DRAFTING_TASK_TYPES is the set feature_compose and patch_with_tools. Excluding drafting from IMMEDIATE grading is CORRECT DESIGN - a drafting call that merely returned tells you nothing, so the judgement was deliberately deferred to the reach verdict. The defect is that the deferred path was never wired: gradeArmByExecution and recordArmOutcomeFromPending have zero non-definition references fleet-wide and their pending ledger was never created. CONSEQUENCE STATED PRECISELY: model selection for code drafting is driven by a posterior that contains ZERO drafting evidence. Whatever arm wins a drafting call wins it on reputation earned at reach_verification, doctor_probe and similar - tasks with different failure modes entirely. This is strictly worse than the earlier framing of graded-on-call-returned, because drafting is not mis-graded, it is UNGRADED. CLOSURE CHECK, SHARPENED: read the live llmModelPolicy and assert that at least one arm carries a non-empty task_alpha or task_beta entry for feature_compose; the gap remains open while all thirteen arms carry per-task posteriors for seven other task types and none for the two that author code.
